crime: Every afternoon during free time, the girl from the next cell found {WITCH_NAME} in the courtyard and asked her to be the pillow from home, the one with her name stitched on it. She couldn't sleep in her cell at night. {WITCH_NAME} became that pillow, stitched name and all, and her neighbor slept face down, hugging her. It was the only time anyone held her.

At home, her mother had only ever said her name to send her to fetch something. Once her little sister was old enough to fetch, her mother stopped saying it. She learned that if no one needs you, no one sees you.
Then, at lunch in the dining hall, her neighbor promised to stop asking. She would sleep on her own folded arm. "You're my friend, not my pillow."
That afternoon at free time, her neighbor lay down by the fountain without asking, her head on her folded arm, and left {WITCH_NAME} standing there with no one holding her.

{WITCH_NAME} begged her to ask just once more. Her neighbor asked for the pillow from home one last time and fell asleep face down on it. Then the pillow closed around her face, over her nose and mouth, and held on until she was still.
At half past two, the prisoners at the upper railing looked down and saw her asleep by the fountain, alone, with no one near her.

At the end of free time, a prisoner turned her over. Pressed into her cheek in stitch marks was her own name, backward. The prisoner understood then: the pillow from home had been {WITCH_NAME}, asked for one last time.
fields.epitaph: The only one who ever wanted her for nothing was the one she would not let go.
execution: In the trial court, a stitched cloth figure stands with open arms, and she is strapped upright against its chest. The figure closes its arms around her, and the embrace tightens on her ribs. She lays her cheek on its stitched shoulder, held at last, and by a thing. The arms stay closed, and everything goes still.

magic.name: Yours for the Asking
magic.text: She can turn into a living version of any object someone asks her for.
